In [[geometry]] and [[topology]], a '''formal manifold''' can mean one of a number of related concepts:
* In the sense of [[Dennis Sullivan]], a formal manifold is one whose real [[homotopy type]] is a formal consequence of its real [[cohomology ring]]; algebro-topologically this means in particular that all [[Massey product]]s vanish.<ref>{{cite book|last=Sullivan|first=Dennis|authorlink=Dennis Sullivan|contribution=Differential forms and the topology of manifolds|title=Manifolds—Tokyo 1973 (Proc. Internat. Conf., Tokyo, 1973) |pages= 37–49|publisher=[[University of Tokyo Press]]|location= Tokyo|year= 1975|mr=0370611|zbl=0319.58005}}</ref>
* A stronger notion is a geometrically formal manifold, a manifold on which all [[wedge product]]s of [[harmonic form]]s are harmonic.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Kotschick|first= Dieter|authorlink=Dieter Kotschick|title= On products of harmonic forms|journal=[[Duke Mathematical Journal]]|volume= 107|issue=3|pages=521–531|year=2001|mr=1828300|doi=10.1215/S0012-7094-01-10734-5|arxiv=math/0004009}}</ref>
